claims.text: The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy with Ti additions is a supersaturated solid solution without significant precipitate formation.
The proposed intervention consists of solutionizing, room-temperature deformation, aging at approximately 800°C for 2 hours in a controlled atmosphere, and controlled cooling.
The thermomechanical aging treatment will induce in-situ TiC nanoprecipitation in the alloy.
The resulting TiC nanoprecipitates will be uniformly dispersed and coherent with the alloy matrix.
The TiC nanoprecipitates will form an interconnected network within the alloy matrix.
TiC nanoprecipitates will act as high-thermal-conductivity bridges in the CoCrFeMnNi-based matrix.
The TiC bridges will enhance phonon transport through the alloy.
The TiC bridges will enhance electron transport through the alloy.
Coherent TiC–matrix interfaces will maintain efficient mechanical load transfer.
Coherent TiC–matrix interfaces will improve resistance to creep at high temperature and under cyclic loading.
The treated alloy will have higher effective thermal conductivity than untreated CoCrFeMnNi alloy with Ti additions.
The treated alloy will maintain or increase mechanical strength relative to the untreated alloy under high-temperature cyclic stresses.
The predicted improvement is intended to hold during transient thermal exposures up to 800°C with cyclic mechanical stresses.
Thermal and mechanical improvement depends on achieving a uniform nanoprecipitate distribution through precise process control.
Deviations in carbon content or aging kinetics may produce nonuniform precipitates and local mechanical weaknesses.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant thermal-conductivity improvement, or degradation of strength or creep resistance, would falsify the hypothesis.
